```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 8
    n_vehicles = 3
    Q = 51  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[54, 33], [63, 77], [23, 84], [75, 18], [8, 71], [94, 52], [58, 77], [51, 55]]
    demands = [12, 9, 10, 13, 12, 6, 19, 21]
    time_windows = [[0, 294], [37, 98], [36, 89], [59, 135], [46, 103], [48, 119], [41, 104], [25, 112], [7, 71]]
    service_times = [11, 11, 13, 7, 11, 13, 5, 9]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Memo: Vehicle Routing and Scheduling Challenge

To: Dispatch Planning and Fleet Supervisors
From: Logistics Operations Manager
Subject: Single-trip routing plan with time windows and capacity limits

Context
We are planning the next delivery cycle from our central facility using a small fleet of identical vehicles. All vehicles will start from the depot at time 0, perform a single continuous tour (no mid-shift returns or second runs), and must be back at the depot before it closes. The customer set for this cycle is fixed and each location must receive exactly one visit.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
- Each assigned vehicle departs at time 0, visits an ordered sequence of customer stops, and returns to the depot before closing.
- Travel time between any two locations is the straight-line distance between their coordinates. We assume a speed of 1 unit of distance per unit of time, so travel time and distance are interchangeable.
- Every customer has a specific time window, defined by an earliest and latest acceptable start-of-service. If a driver arrives early, the vehicle must wait until the window opens before unloading begins.
- Each stop requires a defined unloading/service time. The vehicle departs a customer when service is complete. If the vehicle had to wait for the window to open, departure follows the window opening plus service time; otherwise, it follows arrival time plus service time.
- Vehicles are capacity-constrained. The cumulative quantity loaded on any vehicle at any point in its tour must not exceed its capacity. No split deliveries are allowed; each customer is served in full during a single visit by one vehicle.

Cost Considerations
- Using a vehicle triggers a fixed deployment cost, independent of distance traveled.
- Travel cost is proportional to total distance driven.
- Our planning should weigh whether the marginal savings in distance justify deploying an additional vehicle, while always meeting service commitments.

Goal
Design a set of single-trip routes that:
- Assign every customer to exactly one vehicle, with no omissions or repeats.
- Respect customer time windows, including waiting when arriving early.
- Include the required service time at each stop and return each vehicle to the depot before closing.
- Keep total load on each vehicle within its capacity at all times.
- Minimize the sum of total distance traveled and fixed deployment costs.

Expected Planning Output
- Route assignments and customer visit sequences for each deployed vehicle.
- Planned arrival, service start, and departure times at each stop, including any necessary waiting.
- Load profile along each route to verify capacity compliance.
- Estimated total distance and total cost of the overall plan.
